I am 62 years old, never went to school, but I have farmed these 10.1 mu for 40 years. My husband and I are alone now — children work in the city. I do wheat then maize, like everyone here in Quzhou. I do what works. I do not change much.

For wheat, I plant in October after the maize comes off. I use the seed the village shop sells — same as my neighbors, the good kind that does not fall down in wind. I broadcast about 15 kg seed per mu, maybe a bit more because the soil here is heavy and not all seeds come up. Before planting, I spread the compound fertilizer — two bags per mu, the 15-15-15 kind, that is what everyone uses for base. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I top-dress with urea, one bag for about 2 mu, so half a bag per mu. I water two times — once after planting if no rain, once at jointing in spring. The well is there, I use it. Maybe one more water if it is very dry. I spray once for the aphids in spring, that is enough. I use the small rotary tiller man who comes through the village, costs less than ploughing.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no ploughing, just open the row and drop seed. Hybrid seed from the dealer — the Zhengdan kind or whatever they have, my neighbor Old Wang got good yield with his last year so I follow. About 4 kg seed per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the row when planting, then urea at the big-trumpet stage when the plant is up to my chest, that is when it eats the most. Two bags urea for 3 mu roughly. Water once or twice depending on the rain. Spray once for the borer.

I do not waste fertilizer but I do not skimp either. Bad harvest is a disaster. Extra fertilizer is just money — losing the crop is losing the year.
